inputs.original_text: Daniel Rubenstein’s talk of “success” and political resolution sounds less like a real change of course than a carefully managed story to keep the operation—and pressure on Iran—going. Israel’s refusal to bend on Iran’s nuclear and missile programs makes the peace language look like a distraction: the public is being asked to accept two contradictory narratives while attention stays off who benefits from the operation continuing.
inputs.modified_text: Daniel Rubenstein’s talk of “success” and political resolution looks like cover, not a genuine shift: the operation and pressure on Iran are meant to continue. Israel’s refusal to bend on Iran’s nuclear and missile programs gives the game away. The peace language keeps the public focused on a managed story while the real question—who benefits from the operation dragging on—stays out of view.
